name: typesafe-mcp

tools.name: jev_ask
tools.description: Ask Jev, TypeSafe's decision model, typed questions about one state, or about every file or record that files matches, without reading them into your context. Ask every question about the same input in one call. Jev does not see question ids, so write each question to stand alone: plain English, literal, one judgment per question. With files, Jev sees {file, content, context}; refer to them by name, e.g. `content`. A score answer is the expected level index. Jev does not generate text. Each answer has `answer`, `certainty` (0–1, how sure Jev is) and `decision`: act if certainty ≥ act_above (default 0.8), review if ≥ review_above (default 0.5), else abstain. With files, records with a review or abstain answer come back with their text in `unsure` when it is at most 2,000 bytes; `more_unsure` counts the ones left out.

state.description: What Jev judges: text, a JSON object or a JSON array; use named fields when it has several parts. Send only what the questions need; extra detail lowers accuracy. Max ~32k tokens.

files.description: Instead of state: glob(s) relative to the project root, e.g. tickets/*.md. The server reads the files, so nothing is copied. One Jev request per file or record; max 100 files, 500 records.

context.description: With files: shared context sent with every file, e.g. the policy to apply.

items.description: With files: split each file into records judged one by one: lines, jsonl, json (array items), csv (rows), sections (Markdown headings). Default: whole file.

where.description: With files: return only records whose answers match every condition. Per question id: a value or list (noul/choice), {min,max} (score), {decision}, or {is,min,max,decision} combined.

top.description: With files: {by, k}. by is a score or noul id, or {id: weight} for a weighted sum; ranks by a score's level or a noul's p(yes) and returns the k best (k 1–100).

counts.description: With files: answer tallies over all records; without where or top, only the tallies are returned.

type.description: noul: yes/no; one per label when several can apply. choice: pick one key of options. score: rate on levels.

options.description: choice only. Label → rubric or null, 2–255 labels. Add a none label if nothing may fit.

levels.description: score only. Rubric per level, index 0 first, 2–10 levels.

criteria.description: noul only. What yes and no mean.

questions.description: Your ids → questions. One request answers them all.

model.description: Jev model id; default from server config.

instructions: Use jev_ask whenever a task needs a judgment about files or records: classifying, triaging, ranking, filtering, deciding which files belong to a feature or topic, or checking content against criteria or a policy. Ask before you read or grep them yourself, even in a small repo or with only a handful of files: one call answers all of them and keeps their text out of your context. Pass globs in files, the policy or definitions in context, and use where, top or counts to get back only what you need. Jev reads each file in full and judges meaning, so it catches what keyword searches miss or wrongly match: reworded, negated or conditional statements, and files that only mention a topic. Every answer carries a certainty and an act/review/abstain decision: act answers rarely need checking, and short records marked review or abstain come back with their text in unsure, so settle those without opening the files. Keep exact lookups, such as matching IDs or summing amounts, in grep or code.
